stories.notes: Cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) feature with empty acceptance criteria and null spec — no prior hand-curation detected. openspec must elaborate requirements and draft ACs first; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage. High priority due to zero existing specification and multi-platform scope.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability — no existing code provides real-time CMS content updates. The attachment point is useContent, the single hook through which all 236+ components fetch Contentstack content via getContentByKey. Live Preview SDK integration must plug into this layer (or the provider/context backing it) to subscribe to preview content changes and trigger re-renders. Since ACs are empty, VCs derive solely from the description.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all criteria above are new. I could not read the actual file contents (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentCard.ts), which limits precision around the existing API surface — some ACs may need adjustment once the actual hook signature, service methods, and interface shapes are known. Key design decisions reflected in the ACs: (1) Live Preview must be opt-in and gated from production (AC-3, AC-4, AC-16) to prevent security and performance regressions; (2) graceful degradation is required for disconnection, malformed data, and SDK unavailability (AC-5, AC-6, AC-9, AC-10, AC-16); (3) subscription lifecycle must be managed to avoid leaks on route changes (AC-15); (4) cross-site parity is explicit since GO, UP, and MX share the same file structure (AC-13); (5) accessibility after re-render is required (AC-14); (6) rich-text/modular-block edge case is included because Contentstack content often uses these (AC-17).

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the architectural integration point (useContent hook) and the 236+ component surface area, while speckit contributed security gating, graceful degradation, subscription lifecycle, and cross-site parity design decisions. However, two concerns warrant human review. First, openspec's coordinator instructions were to 'elaborate requirements and draft ACs first,' yet acceptanceChanged is false — it provided architectural context but did not formally produce acceptance criteria. Second, speckit states 'all criteria above are new' (implying it authored ACs) while also reporting acceptanceChanged: false, a contradiction that suggests either the ACs were written but not flagged, or speckit's notes reference ACs that aren't reflected in the structured output. Additionally, speckit could not read the actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, etc.), limiting precision of its recommendations. The collaborative work is directionally sound but the AC authorship chain is unclear and needs a human to confirm the criteria are properly captured.
